Hi Alex — thanks for the clear ask and the SOW. High-level answers below; happy to get on a quick call to walk through numbers.

1) Licensing unit: two supported patterns —
   - Per-site license (recommended for predictable, multi-site installs): flat fee per site + per-GPU additive for high-throughput nodes. Good for customers who want a simple invoice line per location.
   - Per-GPU/node license: metered per-GPU monthly charge. Better if you expect to scale GPU counts per location and want elasticity.

2) Platform fee: we can offer either:
   - One-time upfront platform fee (larger discount at commit), or
   - Amortized monthly across a defined period (6 or 12 months) — common for procurement teams that prefer OPEX treatment.

Support tiers: Standard (S0) = 9x5, Premium (S1) = 24x7 with 4-hour escalations, Enterprise (S2) = named SRE + on-call rotations.

Pilot credits: we typically provide a pilot credit; 10% is standard, 15–20% is possible for multi-site rollouts tied to a 12–24 month commitment.

Suggested next step: I can draft two price sketches for your 25-site scenario: (A) Per-site primary license + 1 GPU included, burst GPU add-on; (B) Per-GPU monthly model. Which would procurement prefer? If you want amortized platform fee, confirm 6 vs 12 months.

I copied a short pricing grid (attached) and propose a follow-up call tomorrow afternoon.

Grace / Marissa — quick pricing ops guidance:

- Approve pilot discount but cap at 15% first-year effective discount (we can structure to front-load credit in month 1–3). 20% is aggressive for a 25-site commercial roll.
- Platform fee amortization: OK to support 6 months for pilot customers, but for a committed commercial deal we should push to 12 months amortization if the deal value exceeds $250k ARR equivalent. - Licensing: per-site + included 1 GPU works for bookkeeping and is simpler for procurement; offer per-GPU as an alternate with slightly higher unit rate.

If legal needs to split line items, finance can map the amortized platform fee to monthly invoices (we'll generate an invoice schedule).

I will authorize the 15% pilot credit and 12-month amortization by default unless procurement insists on 6 months.
